i0: **Reported speech** (or indirect speech) is how we tell someone what another person said, without using their exact words: *“I'm tired.” → She **said** (that) she **was** tired.*
i1: The main changes are the **tense**, **pronouns** and **time words**. For other reporting verbs (*promise, suggest, warn*), see [Reporting Verbs](/blog/grammar/reporting-verbs/).
rs-said-told.t: Say or tell? She said / She told me
rs-said-told.s: **say** + (that) + what: *She said (that) she was hungry.* **tell + person** + (that): *She told me (that) she was hungry.*
rs-said-told.b1: ***Tell*** needs a **person** after it: *tell me, tell him, tell the class*. ***Say*** doesn't: *say something*. If you want a person after *say*, use *to*: *He **said to** me…*
rs-said-told.b2: ***That*** is optional after both: *She said **(that)** she was busy.*
rs-said-told.b3: Fixed phrases with *tell*: *tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke, tell the time*. With *say*: *say hello, say goodbye, say sorry, say something / nothing*.
rs-backshift.s: When the reporting verb is past (*said, told*), the tense usually moves **one step back**: *“I'm tired” → She said she **was** tired. “I'll call” → He said he **would** call.*
rs-backshift.b0.3.1: past perfect: *She said she **had lost** it.* (or *lost*)
rs-backshift.b0.6.0: am going to: *“I**'m going to** move.”*
rs-backshift.b0.6.1: was going to: *He said he **was going to** move.*
rs-backshift.b1: Pronouns also change to fit the new speaker: *“**I** love **my** job.” → She said **she** loved **her** job.*
rs-backshift.b2: The past simple can stay the same in reported speech when the time is clear: *She said she **lost** / **had lost** her keys yesterday.*
rs-no-backshift.s: Don't change the tense when the reporting verb is **present** (*She says she's tired*) or, optionally, when the situation is **still true**: *He said he lives in Paris.*
rs-no-backshift.b0: If the reporting verb is in the **present** (*says, tells, thinks*), the tense doesn't change: *My doctor **says** I **need** more rest.*
rs-no-backshift.b1: If the statement is **still true** now, you can keep the original tense: *“I'm a vegetarian.” → She said she **is** a vegetarian.* (She still is.) Both *is* and *was* are correct here.
rs-no-backshift.b2: General truths usually keep the present: *The teacher said that water **boils** at 100°C.*
rs-no-backshift.b3: When in doubt, backshift. It's always correct after a past reporting verb if the statement was true at that time.
rs-time-place.t: Time and place words: tomorrow → the next day
rs-time-place.s: When the time or place has changed, words like **now, today, tomorrow, here, this** change too: *“I'll see you tomorrow.” → He said he'd see me **the next day**.*
rs-time-place.b0.2.1: the day before / the previous day
rs-time-place.b0.3.1: the next day / the following day
rs-time-place.b0.4.1: the week before / the previous week
rs-time-place.b1: Only change these words if the time or place is **different** when you report. If you report on the same day, *“I'll call you tomorrow”* can stay *He said he'd call me **tomorrow***.
rs-questions.t: Reported questions: He asked me where I lived
rs-questions.s: Reported questions use **statement word order** and no *do / did*: *“Where do you live?” → He asked me where I **lived**.* Yes/no questions use **if / whether**.
rs-questions.b1: In reported questions: no question word order, no *do / does / did*, no question mark: *She asked where **the station was**.* Not *She asked where was the station?*
rs-questions.b2: The tense changes in the same way as statements (backshift).
rs-orders-requests.t: Reported orders and requests: told me to, asked me not to
rs-orders-requests.s: **tell / ask + person + (not) to + verb**: *“Sit down.” → She told me **to sit** down. “Please don't shout.” → He asked us **not to** shout.*
rs-orders-requests.b1: Use ***tell*** for orders and instructions, and ***ask*** for requests. The negative is ***not to*** + verb (not *to don't*).
x.rs-backshift-s03: Present perfect → past perfect (*lost* is also common).
x.rs-no-backshift-s02: A general truth: the present is normal (*was* is also possible).
